name: Sky as Nature: Free Selection and Ratings
description: Is the sky part of nature? Participants click every area of a photograph they consider nature, then rate it on five sliders: familiarity, naturalness (0–100), openness of the view, relaxed–stressed and preference (−50 to 50). 96 images per participant: 48 environments (12 urban, 12 some urban, 12 some nature, 12 nature) from two vantage points each, with one of three horizon levels (low, medium, high) per image, balanced to 8 images per environment type × horizon cell. Selection uses a 150-pixel circle on the 1500 × 750 image, 15 s per image, Next after 5 s. Click coordinates, horizon and timing are recorded per image for overlaying on semantic segmentation (sky, trees, water, …). Stimuli: the authors' 288 crops (OSF osf.io/w9rcq) of CC0 HDRI panoramas from Poly Haven, as in the paper. Rebuilt from Sztuka et al. (2022), Frontiers in Psychology 13: 932507. Differences from the original study: (1) the pre-task questionnaires (socio-economic status, living conditions, STAI, BFI-10, AREA, connectedness to nature) are left out; only gender and age are asked; (2) the paper does not say where the naturalness slider starts, so it starts at the midpoint (50); the other sliders start at 0 as in the paper; (3) images are stored as JPEG at quality 80.
author: Sztuka, Örken, Sudimac & Kühn

elements.description: One record per image: key = environment_category_vantage (e.g. canary_wharf_U_1), shown = the image file (its name carries the horizon level L/M/H). value = { environment, category (U, SU, SN, N), horizon (L, M, H), vantage (1 front, 2 back), clicks: [[x, y], ...] with x and y as fractions of image width and height from the top-left corner, radius: 0.1 (circle radius as a fraction of image width, i.e. 150 px on the 1500 × 750 original), seconds: time on the selection screen, timedOut: true when the 15 s ran out }.

config.description: Free-selection task and five ratings on 96 scenes, rebuilt from Sztuka, Örken, Sudimac and Kühn (2022), “The other blue: Role of sky in the perception of nature”, Frontiers in Psychology. 48 environments (12 urban, 12 some urban, 12 some nature, 12 nature), each shown from two vantage points (front, back). For each image the participant sees one of three horizon levels (low, medium, high), balanced so that every participant sees 8 images in each environment type × horizon cell. On each image the participant clicks the areas they consider nature (a 150-pixel circle on a 1500-pixel-wide image, any number of clicks, 15 s, Next unlocks after 5 s), then rates the image.
